projects.title: Portfolio Optimization
projects.decision: How much of each asset to hold, and how often to rebalance.
projects.hard_part: Mean-variance weights are notoriously unstable because sample covariance is badly conditioned. Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage and risk parity are included precisely to show the instability and what damps it, with walk-forward rebalancing so the result is out-of-sample.

projects.title: Credit Risk Scorecard
projects.decision: Approve, decline, or price a loan application.
projects.hard_part: A regulated decision has to be explainable, so the model is a WOE/IV scorecard with monotonic binning translated into integer points -- and the accuracy given up relative to raw boosting is measured rather than assumed.

projects.title: Card Fraud Detection
projects.decision: Block, review, or allow a transaction in real time.
projects.hard_part: At 0.2% positives, accuracy and ROC-AUC are both misleading, and velocity features leak the future unless they are computed strictly backwards. PR-AUC plus an explicit cost matrix decides the threshold.

projects.title: Fraud Ring Detection on Graphs
projects.decision: Which accounts to investigate together, rather than one at a time.
projects.hard_part: A ring is invisible per-account and obvious as a subgraph, so detection is community structure: IDF-weighted bipartite projection, Louvain modularity from scratch, and label propagation. Modularity's resolution limit is demonstrated rather than glossed over, because it silently hides small rings inside large communities.

projects.title: Churn Prediction Service
projects.decision: Which customers to spend retention budget on.
projects.hard_part: A ranked list is not a decision. Probabilities are calibrated and the threshold comes from expected value given the offer cost and the margin saved, then served behind an API with the same preprocessing as training.

projects.title: A/B Testing Engine
projects.decision: Ship the variant, or do not.
projects.hard_part: Fixed-horizon p-values are invalid the moment somebody peeks, which everybody does. Always-valid sequential tests, CUPED variance reduction, sample-ratio-mismatch gating and FDR control across metric families -- with a simulator that scores the analysis method itself for false positive rate.

projects.title: Uplift Modeling
projects.decision: Who to target, given that most responders would have converted anyway.
projects.hard_part: The individual treatment effect is never observed, so no row has a label. S/T/X/R-learners and the transformed outcome make it estimable, and Qini curves evaluate ranking without ground truth.

projects.title: Implicit-Feedback Recommender
projects.decision: What to put in front of a user, including one you have never seen.
projects.hard_part: Implicit feedback has no negatives: a non-click is not a dislike. ALS with confidence weighting from scratch, content-based routing for cold start, and business re-ranking for diversity, availability and margin.

projects.title: Bayesian Marketing Mix Modeling
projects.decision: How to split next quarter's budget across channels.
projects.hard_part: Spend is correlated across channels and adstock and saturation are only weakly identified, so point estimates are misleading and the posterior is the deliverable. NUTS-free Metropolis sampling with R-hat and ESS diagnostics, plus an explicit statement that regression on observational spend is not a causal estimate without geo experiments to anchor it.

projects.title: Survival Analysis for Churn
projects.decision: When a customer will leave, not merely whether.
projects.hard_part: Binary churn classification silently throws away censoring: a customer who has not yet churned is not a negative example. Kaplan-Meier with Greenwood intervals, Cox proportional hazards with Efron ties by Newton-Raphson, Schoenfeld residuals to test the proportionality assumption the model depends on, and IPCW Brier scores that stay honest under censoring.

projects.title: Hospital Readmission Risk
projects.decision: Which discharged patients get a follow-up call, given a fixed number of nurses.
projects.hard_part: Capacity is the constraint, not the AUC, so evaluation is a decision curve under a daily call budget -- plus a subgroup audit for calibration and error-rate gaps, because an unequal error rate is a clinical harm.

projects.title: Citation-Verified RAG
projects.decision: Answer the question, or say you cannot.
projects.hard_part: A fluent unsupported answer is worse than no answer. Every claim is verified against its cited span, abstention is calibrated, and retrieval is measured with recall@k, MRR and nDCG on a labelled set.

projects.title: Support Ticket Routing
projects.decision: Which queue a ticket goes to, and when a human decides instead.
projects.hard_part: Random validation flatters a model whose vocabulary drifts weekly, so validation is temporal. Word plus character n-grams survive typos, and a coverage curve shows what accuracy is bought by deferring the least confident share.

projects.title: LLM Eval and Guardrails
projects.decision: Is this prompt or model change a regression?
projects.hard_part: An LLM judge is a measuring instrument, so it is validated against human labels before it is trusted. Paired McNemar tests gate releases, and guardrails fail closed on injection and PII.

projects.title: Transformer From Scratch
projects.decision: None -- this one exists to prove the mechanism is understood, not borrowed.
projects.hard_part: Every backward pass is derived by hand and verified against finite differences: softmax Jacobian, LayerNorm's two correction terms, causal masking, and AdamW's decoupled decay. Byte-level BPE and KV-cache generation included.

projects.title: Search Reranking and Learning to Rank
projects.decision: What order to show results in, learned from logs nobody labelled.
projects.hard_part: Clicks measure attention as much as relevance, so a model trained on raw clicks reproduces the incumbent ranker including the mistakes that never got clicked. Pointwise, RankNet and LambdaRank on one model class isolate the loss, and inverse propensity weighting corrects position bias -- with the propensity estimator's own bias demonstrated rather than hidden.

projects.title: Demand Forecasting and Inventory
projects.decision: How much to reorder, and when.
projects.hard_part: A point forecast cannot set a reorder point; the service level depends on the tail. Quantile forecasts feed reorder points whose achieved service level and holding cost are measured in simulation, with rolling-origin backtesting throughout.

projects.title: Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
projects.decision: Is this deviation worth waking somebody for?
projects.hard_part: Per-signal thresholds miss the anomalies that matter, because a fleet failure is a change in the correlation structure while every individual series stays in range. Mahalanobis distance, PCA reconstruction error and a spectral residual, evaluated with range-based precision and recall plus detection delay -- because point-wise F1 rewards a detector that fires once inside a long event and misses the rest.

projects.title: Vehicle Routing with Time Windows
projects.decision: Which driver visits which stops, in what order.
projects.hard_part: CVRPTW is NP-hard and the constraints interact: a route that respects capacity can violate a time window and vice versa. Clarke-Wright savings for construction, then guided local search over 2-opt, Or-opt and cross-exchange -- with feasibility checked exactly rather than penalised, and the gap to a lower bound reported instead of claiming optimality.

projects.title: Dynamic Pricing with Contextual Bandits
projects.decision: What price to quote this customer, now.
projects.hard_part: A pricing experiment costs money on every impression, so exploration has to be paid for deliberately. LinUCB and linear Thompson sampling with Sherman-Morrison rank-1 updates, cumulative regret against an oracle, and off-policy evaluation (IPS, SNIPS, doubly robust) so a new policy can be judged before it is deployed -- including where each estimator breaks.

projects.title: Vision, Grad-CAM and Distillation
projects.decision: Can this classifier be trusted, and can it run on a small device?
projects.hard_part: A planted background shortcut is inserted deliberately so that Grad-CAM pointing-game scores can catch a model that is right for the wrong reason. Calibration, robustness gaps and 10x distillation are all measured.

projects.title: SQL Analytics Warehouse
projects.decision: What the business actually did last quarter.
projects.hard_part: Cohort retention, RFM, LTV and multi-touch attribution written as window-function SQL against a normalised schema, with reproducible SQL-only seed data and data-quality assertions that fail loudly.

projects.title: Pipeline Orchestration and Data Contracts
projects.decision: Should this data be published at all?
projects.hard_part: Content-addressed fingerprints give incremental runs with early cutoff; contracts validate before publishing and never coerce; PSI bins come from the baseline; and lineage answers 'what else is wrong?' by traversal rather than memory.

projects.title: Feature Store and Point-in-Time Joins
projects.decision: Is this training set actually reproducible in production?
projects.hard_part: Training-serving skew is a correctness bug that no metric reveals: a naive join attaches feature values that did not exist when the label was generated. As-of joins with explicit event-time versus processing-time semantics, late-arriving data, and a skew detector that compares offline and online reads on the same keys.

projects.title: Streaming Event Processor
projects.decision: What the aggregate is right now, when events arrive out of order.
projects.hard_part: Event time and processing time diverge, so a window can never be closed with certainty -- only with a watermark that trades completeness for latency. Tumbling, sliding and session windows over pane decomposition, allowed lateness with explicit retractions, Space-Saving top-k under bounded memory, and checkpoints that make replay idempotent.

projects.title: Drift Monitoring Service
projects.decision: Is the model still fit for production, and is this alert worth waking someone for?
projects.hard_part: A monitor that cries wolf is turned off. PSI/KS/Wasserstein with FDR control and effect-size gating, delayed-label performance tracking, and a harness that scores the monitor itself on detection delay against false alarms.

projects.title: Differential Privacy for Tabular ML
projects.decision: Can this model be released without leaking the people in it?
projects.hard_part: Epsilon is a bound on a mechanism, not a measurement of leakage, and the guarantee is void if sensitivity is mis-stated -- so clipping bias and small-cell error are shown alongside it. RDP accounting for the subsampled Gaussian, DP-SGD with per-example clipping, and a membership-inference audit whose empirical epsilon is reported next to the accounted one, in both directions: a successful attack proves a leak, a failed attack proves only that this attack failed.
